chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to me that Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to him, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Saif ibn Amirah, from Zaid al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever says 'Praise be to Allah as He deserves', Allah will keep the scribes of heaven busy. It was asked, 'How do the scribes of the heavens remain busy?' He said, 'They say, O Allah! We do not know the unseen.' So Allah says, 'Write it as my servant said it, and for him is its reward.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of saying 'Praise be to Allah as He deserves' according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the profound inadequacy of human language in capturing the infinite majesty of Allah, a concept central to Shia theological reflections on divine transcendence (Tanzih). The celestial scribes' uncertainty illustrates the gap between created perception and divine reality, prompting Allah to validate the servant's intent by accepting their declaration as the definitive measure of reward. This emphasizes the Shia scholarly view that sincere, albeit linguistically limited, devotion is elevated by Divine command to its full spiritual potential.
